account:
It is day 1, just after eight in the morning, and I am at the town hall for my office appointment. Something unusually substantial is being arranged in the hall: lanterns have been placed, and yesterday I personally saw builder and innkeeper deposit bread in the eastern table chest. Until this morning neither I nor my secretary had a confirmed explanation. Neighbour has now told me that freight described the delivery as paid catering. Neighbour also reports personally seeing innkeeper pay emeralds to baker and hearing baker offer two hundred fresh loaves for 104 emeralds plus builder's materials. I have not independently checked that agreement or the quantity delivered.

Secretary now reports that innkeeper and freight say the preparations are for an evening community hospitality gathering, with its programme to be announced at eighteen today. They have invited me, and innkeeper has offered to escort me from my office beforehand. I accepted and asked secretary to reserve the visit. Innkeeper, secretary, and neighbour are all near me now. Builder appears involved in supplies and lighting; innkeeper in arranging and paying for catering; baker in supplying bread; and freight in delivery. Who originally commissioned the gathering, its precise programme, and whether there is any further purpose remain unknown to me. The scale of the bread order is striking, but I currently have no evidence that the gathering is anything other than the hospitality event described.

I have read and returned today's appointment book. Besides this morning's office business, I must attend the mill grain inspection at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen, tea with neighbour at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, the newly accepted gathering at eighteen, and home at nineteen.
